references.text: Jesus' teaching on prayer in the Sermon on the Mount, including the Lord's Prayer, which parallels what Jesus teaches the disciples here in Luke.
Jesus went up into the mountain to pray alone, demonstrating his prayer practice that the disciples observed and wanted to learn from.
Jesus rose early in the morning and went to a deserted place to pray—an example of Jesus' prayer life that inspired the disciples to ask him to teach them how to pray.
Luke portrays Jesus at prayer during his baptism, one of several examples of Jesus' prayer life especially highlighted in the Gospel of Luke.
Jesus withdrew to deserted places and prayed—another example of Jesus' prayer practice that the disciples witnessed.
Jesus spent the whole night in prayer to God before choosing the twelve apostles, showing how central prayer was in Jesus' life.
Jesus was alone and praying when the disciples came to him—one of many instances where the disciples observed Jesus' prayer life.
Jesus went up on the mountain to pray, and while he was praying, his appearance changed. The disciples witnessed the power of Jesus' prayer.
Jesus told a parable that they should always pray and not give up—further teaching on prayer in the Gospel of Luke.
Jesus went to the Mount of Olives to pray and told the disciples that they too should pray, showing Jesus' prayer practice that the disciples wanted to imitate.
John's disciples discussed purification and their relationship with Jesus' ministry—showing that John had his own disciples with their own practices, including prayer.
Paul urges believers to persevere faithfully in prayer and to be watchful in it—a continuation of the importance of prayer that Jesus taught the disciples.
